name: atari800
why: An Atari 8-bit emulator opens a door into vintage hardware and running old software from ROM images.

brief.what_it_is: Atari800 is a free, portable emulator of Atari 8-bit computers (400/800, XL/XE and related models) and the Atari 5200 game console. You give it files such as disk images (ATR, XFD, ATX and others), programs (COM, EXE, XEX, BAS), cartridge images (CAR/CART, raw ROM), tape images (CAS) or saved emulator states, and it runs them on an emulated machine with video, sound, joystick and mouse emulation. It builds for many platforms, with SDL2 recommended for desktop use (Linux, macOS, Windows), plus curses text-mode, X11, DOS, Amiga, Android and others. The Homebrew formula also lists a second executable named 'cart', which I did not find described in any page I fetched.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says the main objective is 'to create a freely distributable portable emulator (i.e. with source code available)'. The project began as David Firth's 1995 GPL emulator, and after no new versions appeared after 1997, several developers resumed work on the v0.8.0 source, which Petr Stehlik now maintains.

commands_seen.context: Basic usage line from DOC/USAGE. Filenames are mounted in order: the first disk image goes to drive 1, the next to drive 2, and so on.
Option that inserts a cartridge image (CART or raw format).
Option that runs an Atari program (EXE, COM, XEX, BAS, LST).
Option that attaches a cassette image and boots it.
Option that loads a saved-state file.
Option that turns mouse emulation off. Other values listed in USAGE include pad, touch, koala, pen, gun, amiga, st, trak and joy.
Option that runs the emulator at maximum speed. F12 toggles turbo mode at runtime.
Option that uses a specified configuration file instead of the default.

brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install, the docs say that some OS and hardware features need ROM images that the project does not ship: the MIO and Black Box sections state 'You need ROM images (not provided.)', and OS or BASIC ROMs are supplied with -osa_rom, -osb_rom, -xlxe_rom, -5200_rom and -basic_rom. Black Box and MIO also need a blank SCSI disk image, which the docs say can be made with dd. Settings can be saved with -autosave-config, and the default is -no-autosave-config. I did not see a separate first-run walkthrough, and the README points to DOC/README, DOC/INSTALL and DOC/USAGE for platform-specific steps. I only fetched USAGE, not INSTALL.
brief.standout: It emulates a very wide range of Atari hardware in one program, including 80-column boards, the XEP80, Voice Box, Black Box, MIO and several mouse and light-pen peripherals, and it is GPL with a long history. The NTSC artifacting and colour-adjustment options, plus Alt-based hotkeys for monitor, tape and disk management, are unusually detailed.
brief.status: Maintained, judging by the evidence. The README names version 7.2.1, the GitHub repo shows 3,161 commits, 431 stars and 119 forks, and the homepage copyright runs '2002 - 2026'. I did not see a last-release date or last-commit date, so the exact recency is unknown.
brief.caveats: Several hardware and OS features need ROM images the user must supply. The docs say the 1450XLD and MIO/Black Box options conflict with the OS patches and need -nopatchall. Tape saving only works at the standard 600 baud, copy-protected tapes that depend on non-standard signals are not supported, and saving state during a tape operation is not restored properly. The curses build lacks F10 screenshots and Shift+F5/Shift+F10. The license is GPL-2.0. The brew caveats field is empty. The 'cart' executable named in the formula was not described in anything I read.
quotes: This is a free and portable Atari 8-bit computer and 5200 console emulator, originally written by David Firth and now developed by the Atari800 Development Team
Our main objective is to create a freely distributable portable emulator (i.e. with source code available).
fetch_log: https://atari800.github.io/ - worked; homepage text with feature list, history and menu, no direct README links
https://github.com/atari800/atari800 - worked; README for version 7.2.1 that points to DOC/ files for install and usage
https://github.com/atari800/atari800/blob/master/DOC/USAGE - worked; full command-line options, file types and keyboard map

judge.reason: A portable emulator for a whole family of Atari computers and their unusual peripherals makes vintage hardware and software directly explorable, beyond just replaying console games.

entry.title: atari800
entry.tldr: A free emulator of the Atari 400/800, XL/XE computers and the 5200 console that runs disk, cartridge, tape and program images.
entry.deeper_look:
Atari800 emulates the Atari 8-bit home computers (400/800, XL/XE and related models) and the Atari 5200 console. You hand it files: disk images (ATR, XFD, ATX), programs (COM, EXE, XEX, BAS), cartridge images, cassette images (CAS) or saved emulator states. It runs them on an emulated machine with video, sound, joystick and mouse emulation. SDL2 is the recommended build for desktop use, but the source also targets curses text mode, X11, DOS, Amiga, Android and others.

The project began as David Firth's GPL emulator in 1995. No new versions appeared after 1997, so several developers picked up the v0.8.0 source and carried it forward. Petr Stehlik now maintains it. The homepage states the aim plainly: "Our main objective is to create a freely distributable portable emulator (i.e. with source code available)."

The door it opens is old hardware seen from the inside. The emulator covers a wide range of peripherals: 80-column boards, the XEP80, Voice Box, Black Box, MIO, and several mouse and light-pen types. It also has detailed NTSC artifacting and colour-adjustment options. Running the same software through different emulated configurations shows how much of that era's behaviour depended on the exact machine, the OS ROM, and even the TV.

The formula also installs a second executable named cart. The brief did not find it described anywhere, so this entry does not say what it does.
entry.install:
brew install atari800
# Some OS and hardware features need ROM images the project does not ship. Supply them with -osa_rom, -osb_rom, -xlxe_rom, -5200_rom and -basic_rom.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the command-line options so you can see what the emulator can be told to do.
Runs an Atari program file (EXE, COM, XEX, BAS or LST) on the emulated machine.
Mounts the disk image in drive 1 and runs the emulator at maximum speed. F12 toggles turbo at runtime.

entry.whats_unique: One program covers a very wide range of Atari 8-bit hardware and peripherals, from the 5200 console to the XEP80 and Black Box. Its NTSC artifacting and colour options are unusually detailed.
entry.caveats: Some OS and hardware features need ROM images you must supply yourself, and tape support is limited to standard 600 baud without copy-protected tapes.
